description: MAP log-lik probes on experiment2 data of many one-change refinements of the Erlang incumbent; most add nothing
metadata:
  type: project
---
Experiment 2 (2026-10-30, iter_0 candidate_5): incumbent erlang_interval_size_family_prior MAP log-lik -2246.17 (per-set constant rate -2380, saturated -1787; members of the example set get only 62% yes, so the data are very noisy).
Each change below was added alone to the incumbent: lapse to 0.5 (lapse went to 0), learned example reliability (stayed at 0.90), learned weak/strong sampling mix (theta 0.9, slightly worse), offset arithmetic progressions (weight went to 0, even though many exp2 sets share a residue mod 3/4/5/6/12), digit-vocabulary concepts (weight went to 0), log-scale interval widths (-2262, much worse), Gamma shape on the width prior (no gain). None of these helps.
Primes in their own family on top of powers_own_family gained +0.35 nats; it was submitted as primes_own_family_erlang_interval.
**Why:** these probes save repeating dead ends.
**How to apply:** use scratch/resid.py-style find_MAP probes before writing a candidate. Gains probably need a different decision or noise structure, not more concepts.

Later probes (iter_0 candidate_4_repair_1): learned reliability (stays 0.9, near-duplicate rejected, RMSE 0.0005), log-odds decision distortion (gamma 1.0, bias 0), posterior/likelihood exponents (tau 1.0), Gamma shape (2.08), decade-aligned interval bonus (-0.87, +0.3 LL but RMSE 0.0019 < 0.002 novelty gate) all fail. One-sided thresholds ([1,n], [m,100]) as their own family: +0.85 LL, RMSE 0.011 vs incumbent; submitted as threshold_concepts_erlang_interval. Use scratch/cmp.py there to get the MAP log-lik and the RMSE against the incumbent together.

Raw exp2 data patterns (iter_1 critique, 2026-10-30): no distance gradient among non-members (near 0.42 vs far 0.40), no parity effect, but a shared last digit with every example gives +0.27. Sets with all examples >=50: targets above max get 14% yes (n=35) vs 45% below min, the opposite of threshold extension. Example members get only 62.5% yes. Consecutive trials on different sets agree 0.565 (carryover).

iter_1 candidate_3 (2026-10-30), probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (MAP LL -2245.33): splitting thresholds into "at most"/"at least" families -2245.31 (nothing); powers own family -2245.19; primes own family -2244.85, RMSE 0.0069 — submitted as threshold_concepts_primes_family. Data layout: 10 participants x 450 trials (rows 0-2249 and 2250-4499 are two stimulus batches, 5 responses per cell); per-participant yes-rate matches the model and lag-1 residual autocorrelation is ~0.02, so per-participant bias and carryover terms are not worth adding. Scripts: iter_1/candidate_3/scratch/res.py (residuals by target position).

Decision-rule probes on threshold incumbent (iter_1 candidate_1, 2026-10-30; MAP LL -2245.33): lapse+free guess rate (lapse 0, also 0 on flat-interval exception_rule_family_prior_2), AND rule m^k (k 1.0), soft threshold on membership (-34 nats), OR rule 1-(1-m)^k (k 1.01, +0.015, RMSE 0.0026 on data rows; submitted as any_of_sampled_concepts_endorsement). The wide-interval family (scale ~66) already absorbs guessing.
Big unmodelled signal: per-participant yes rate is bimodal (5 participants ~0.30, 5 ~0.56; 450 trials each, found from trial_index resets). participant_id is hidden in this run, and design/novelty rows have no trial_index, so a participant-bias model can't be scored from stimulus rows alone.

Similarity probes (iter_1 candidate_0): logistic on exemplar similarity exp(-c_digit*[final digit differs] - c_dist*|t-e|/100). Averaging over examples (NLL 3022) beats summing or max (3052); constant rate 3079; tens-digit match adds nothing once distance is in. So pure-similarity models sit about 780 nats of log-lik behind the concept-learning models (-2246). Submitted as average_digit_magnitude_similarity.

Concept-family probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (iter_1 candidate_2, MAP LL -2245.33): extra families added alone — decades, tens digit, repdigits, two-last-digit unions, |tens-units| difference: weight 0, no gain. Extra multiples (10,13..25): +0.14. Digit sum = s (1..18): +0.41, pool RMSE 0.0072 (passes 0.002 gate); submitted as digit_sum_concepts_threshold_erlang. Probe scripts in /tmp/c2p (mk.py adds a family to the incumbent; nov.py gives novelty-pool RMSE).
Pitfall: model.compile_fn(p_yes, inputs=value_vars) with a dict of MAP values gave wrong p_yes; use p_yes.eval({rv: mp[name]}) over free_RVs instead.

iter_1 candidate_4 probes on threshold_concepts_erlang_interval (MAP LL -2245.33): splitting thresholds into lower/upper families (no gain), within-family rule prior ~ size^gamma (gamma 0.03, no gain), example-position recency weighting (rho 0), no participant-level or lag-1 residual structure, calibration by p-bin is near perfect. Per-example evidence weight k^beta (k = number of examples): beta 0.027, +0.87 LL, RMSE 0.0077, sharply peaked (beta ±0.1 costs 5-15 nats); submitted as set_size_amplified_size_principle. Full-interval tensor version (scratch/order.py there) reproduces the grouped incumbent exactly.

iter_1 candidate_5 probes (2026-10-30): incumbent threshold model MAP -2245.33, well calibrated, per-set deviance z=0.67 overall (fits within chance; participants' yes-rates match too, so no individual-difference signal). Powers-own-family + thresholds: +0.14 only. Weber-scaled + thresholds: no gain. Centre-weighted range sampling (density (u(1-u))^kappa within a range) on erlang base: kappa 0.08, +0.52 over base, RMSE 0.008 vs incumbent; LL falls fast for kappa>0.3. A constant recognition yes-rate for members (0.62) costs 25 nats with pool RMSE 0.061; submitted as recognition_shortcut_for_examples. Members are only 16 of the 512 pool stimuli. Scripts: /tmp/r1/ll.py (MAP LL + pool RMSE for any list of model files; may not persist).

135 models/threshold_concepts_erlang_interval.py
"""Refinement of `erlang_interval_size_family_prior`: one-sided magnitude
thresholds as their own concept family.

People do the same Bayesian concept learning over 45 rules and the intervals of
1..100: the size principle (10% of examples drawn at random from 1..100), a
prior mass per concept family (the exception rules in their own family) and an
Erlang prior s * exp(-s / sigma) over the width of bounded ranges. The one
change: one-sided thresholds ("at least m", i.e. [m, 100], and "at most n",
i.e. [1, n]) are a separate kind of program with their own inferred prior
mass, shared equally among them and exempt from the width prior, so all-large
or all-small example sets generalise to the end of the number line.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
ALPHA = 0.9


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


def family(name):
    if name in ("odd", "even"):
        return 0
    if name.startswith("multiples"):
        return 2
    if name.startswith("ends"):
        return 3
    if name.startswith("contains"):
        return 4
    if name.startswith("powers of 2,"):
        return 5  # gerrymandered exception rules
    return 1  # primes, squares, cubes, powers


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULES = list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_FAMILY = np.array([family(n) for n in _RULES])
FAMILY_SIZE = np.bincount(RULE_FAMILY).astype("float64")
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
RULE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * RULE_MEMBERSHIP / RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
# Bounded ranges [m, n] with 1 < m <= n < 100, and one-sided thresholds [1, n] or [m, 100].
LO, HI = np.array([(m, n) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]).T
THRESHOLD = (LO == 1) | (HI == 100)
INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP = ((NUMBERS[None, :] >= LO[:, None]) & (NUMBERS[None, :] <= HI[:, None])).astype("float64")
INTERVAL_WIDTH = HI - LO + 1
INTERVAL_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP / INTERVAL_WIDTH[:, None] + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
WIDTHS = np.arange(1, 99)  # widths a bounded range can have
N_PER_WIDTH = np.array([np.sum(~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)) for w in WIDTHS], dtype="float64")
N_THRESHOLD = float(THRESHOLD.sum())

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules)
    # Per set, log sum of P(D | range) over the bounded ranges of each width and over
    # all thresholds, and each group's posterior membership of every target (the
    # prior is uniform within a group, so these do not depend on the parameters).
    width_log_evidence = pm.Data("width_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS))))
    width_in_concept = pm.Data("width_in_concept", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS), 100)))
    threshold_log_evidence = pm.Data("threshold_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, 1)), shape=(None, 1))
    threshold_in_concept = pm.Data("threshold_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    # Prior mass of the six rule families, bounded ranges and one-sided thresholds.
    family_weight = pm.Dirichlet("family_weight", a=np.ones(8))
    log_w = pt.log(family_weight)
    # Characteristic width of the Erlang prior over bounded ranges.
    interval_scale = pm.LogNormal("interval_scale", mu=np.log(20.0), sigma=1.0)

    erlang = np.log(WIDTHS) - WIDTHS / interval_scale
    log_per_range = erlang - pt.logsumexp(erlang + np.log(N_PER_WIDTH))

    log_rules = (log_w[:6] - np.log(FAMILY_SIZE))[RULE_FAMILY][None, :] + rule_log_lik
    log_widths = log_w[6] + log_per_range[None, :] + width_log_evidence
    log_thresholds = log_w[7] - np.log(N_THRESHOLD) + threshold_log_evidence
    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_widths, log_thresholds], axis=1)
    posterior = pt.exp(log_joint - pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    in_concept = (
        posterior[:, :N_RULES] @ pt.as_tensor(RULE_MEMBERSHIP)
        + (posterior[:, N_RULES:-1, None] * width_in_concept).sum(axis=1)
        + posterior[:, -1, None] * threshold_in_concept
    )  # (sets, targets)

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def _group(log_lik, membership):
    """Log evidence of a group of equally likely concepts and its membership of each target."""
    top = log_lik.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    weight = np.exp(log_lik - top)
    total = weight.sum(axis=1)
    return np.log(total) + top[:, 0], (weight / total[:, None]) @ membership


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}

"""Refinement of `erlang_interval_size_family_prior`: one-sided magnitude
thresholds as their own concept family.

People do the same Bayesian concept learning over 45 rules and the intervals of
1..100: the size principle (10% of examples drawn at random from 1..100), a
prior mass per concept family (the exception rules in their own family) and an
Erlang prior s * exp(-s / sigma) over the width of bounded ranges. The one
change: one-sided thresholds ("at least m", i.e. [m, 100], and "at most n",
i.e. [1, n]) are a separate kind of program with their own inferred prior
mass, shared equally among them and exempt from the width prior, so all-large
or all-small example sets generalise to the end of the number line.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
ALPHA = 0.9


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


def family(name):
    if name in ("odd", "even"):
        return 0
    if name.startswith("multiples"):
        return 2
    if name.startswith("ends"):
        return 3
    if name.startswith("contains"):
        return 4
    if name.startswith("powers of 2,"):
        return 5  # gerrymandered exception rules
    return 1  # primes, squares, cubes, powers


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULES = list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_FAMILY = np.array([family(n) for n in _RULES])
FAMILY_SIZE = np.bincount(RULE_FAMILY).astype("float64")
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
RULE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * RULE_MEMBERSHIP / RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
# Bounded ranges [m, n] with 1 < m <= n < 100, and one-sided thresholds [1, n] or [m, 100].
LO, HI = np.array([(m, n) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]).T
THRESHOLD = (LO == 1) | (HI == 100)
INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP = ((NUMBERS[None, :] >= LO[:, None]) & (NUMBERS[None, :] <= HI[:, None])).astype("float64")
INTERVAL_WIDTH = HI - LO + 1
INTERVAL_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP / INTERVAL_WIDTH[:, None] + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
WIDTHS = np.arange(1, 99)  # widths a bounded range can have
N_PER_WIDTH = np.array([np.sum(~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)) for w in WIDTHS], dtype="float64")
N_THRESHOLD = float(THRESHOLD.sum())

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules)
    # Per set, log sum of P(D | range) over the bounded ranges of each width and over
    # all thresholds, and each group's posterior membership of every target (the
    # prior is uniform within a group, so these do not depend on the parameters).
    width_log_evidence = pm.Data("width_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS))))
    width_in_concept = pm.Data("width_in_concept", np.zeros((1, len(WIDTHS), 100)))
    threshold_log_evidence = pm.Data("threshold_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, 1)), shape=(None, 1))
    threshold_in_concept = pm.Data("threshold_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    # Prior mass of the six rule families, bounded ranges and one-sided thresholds.
    family_weight = pm.Dirichlet("family_weight", a=np.ones(8))
    log_w = pt.log(family_weight)
    # Characteristic width of the Erlang prior over bounded ranges.
    interval_scale = pm.LogNormal("interval_scale", mu=np.log(20.0), sigma=1.0)

    erlang = np.log(WIDTHS) - WIDTHS / interval_scale
    log_per_range = erlang - pt.logsumexp(erlang + np.log(N_PER_WIDTH))

    log_rules = (log_w[:6] - np.log(FAMILY_SIZE))[RULE_FAMILY][None, :] + rule_log_lik
    log_widths = log_w[6] + log_per_range[None, :] + width_log_evidence
    log_thresholds = log_w[7] - np.log(N_THRESHOLD) + threshold_log_evidence
    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_widths, log_thresholds], axis=1)
    posterior = pt.exp(log_joint - pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1, keepdims=True))

        + (posterior[:, N_RULES:-1, None] * width_in_concept).sum(axis=1)
        + posterior[:, -1, None] * threshold_in_concept

def _group(log_lik, membership):
    """Log evidence of a group of equally likely concepts and its membership of each target."""
    top = log_lik.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    weight = np.exp(log_lik - top)
    total = weight.sum(axis=1)
    return np.log(total) + top[:, 0], (weight / total[:, None]) @ membership

        sel = ~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)
        width_log_evidence[:, i], width_in_concept[:, i] = _group(interval_log_lik[:, sel], INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP[sel])
    threshold_log_evidence, threshold_in_concept = _group(
        interval_log_lik[:, THRESHOLD], INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP[THRESHOLD]
    )
    return {
        "rule_log_lik": np.stack([RULE_LOG_LIK[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique]),
        "width_log_evidence": width_log_evidence,
        "width_in_concept": width_in_concept,
        "threshold_log_evidence": threshold_log_evidence[:, None],
        "threshold_in_concept": threshold_in_concept,
        "row_cell": np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),

thresholds ([1, n], [m, 100], their own family), with a prior mass per concept
family and 10% of examples taken as random draws from 1..100. The one change:
the size principle is weaker for magnitude concepts than for rules. An example
inside a range of size s has probability s^-g * 100^(g-1) under it, with g
learned (g = 1 recovers the incumbent; g = 0 is weak sampling, the range judged
only by whether it covers the examples), while rules keep 1 / |rule|. So ranges
do not shrink onto clustered examples as fast as an ideal learner's would, and
"yes" extends further past the examples' extremes for multi-example sets.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
ALPHA = 0.9


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


def family(name):
    if name in ("odd", "even"):
        return 0
    if name.startswith("multiples"):
        return 2
    if name.startswith("ends"):
        return 3
    if name.startswith("contains"):
        return 4
    if name.startswith("powers of 2,"):
        return 5  # gerrymandered exception rules
    return 1  # primes, squares, cubes, powers


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULES = list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_FAMILY = np.array([family(n) for n in _RULES])
FAMILY_SIZE = np.bincount(RULE_FAMILY).astype("float64")
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")

LO, HI = np.array([(m, n) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]).T
THRESHOLD = (LO == 1) | (HI == 100)
INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP = ((NUMBERS[None, :] >= LO[:, None]) & (NUMBERS[None, :] <= HI[:, None])).astype("float64")
INTERVAL_WIDTH = HI - LO + 1
WIDTHS = np.arange(1, 99)  # widths a bounded range can have
N_PER_WIDTH = np.array([np.sum(~THRESHOLD & (INTERVAL_WIDTH == w)) for w in WIDTHS], dtype="float64")
N_THRESHOLD = float(THRESHOLD.sum())
CONCEPT_MEMBERSHIP = np.vstack([RULE_MEMBERSHIP, INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP])
N_CONCEPTS = len(CONCEPT_MEMBERSHIP)
LOG_RULE_SIZE = np.log(RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1))
LOG_INTERVAL_SIZE = np.log(INTERVAL_WIDTH.astype("float64"))
BOUNDED_WIDTH_INDEX = np.where(THRESHOLD, 0, INTERVAL_WIDTH - 1)

with pm.Model() as model:
    # Per set and concept: how many examples the concept contains and how many it misses.
    n_inside = pm.Data("n_inside", np.zeros((1, N_CONCEPTS)))
    n_outside = pm.Data("n_outside", np.zeros((1, N_CONCEPTS)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    # Prior mass of the six rule families, bounded ranges and one-sided thresholds.
    family_weight = pm.Dirichlet("family_weight", a=np.ones(8))
    log_w = pt.log(family_weight)
    # Characteristic width of the Erlang prior over bounded ranges.
    interval_scale = pm.LogNormal("interval_scale", mu=np.log(20.0), sigma=1.0)
    # Strength of the size principle for ranges and thresholds (1 = as for rules).
    range_size_strength = pm.Beta("range_size_strength", alpha=2.0, beta=2.0)

    # Probability of an example under each concept that contains it.
    log_density = pt.concatenate(
        [-LOG_RULE_SIZE, -range_size_strength * LOG_INTERVAL_SIZE + (range_size_strength - 1) * np.log(100.0)]
    )
    log_in = pt.log(ALPHA * pt.exp(log_density) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
    log_lik = n_inside * log_in[None, :] + n_outside * np.log((1 - ALPHA) / 100)

    erlang = np.log(WIDTHS) - WIDTHS / interval_scale
    log_per_range = erlang - pt.logsumexp(erlang + np.log(N_PER_WIDTH))
    interval_prior = pt.switch(
        THRESHOLD, log_w[7] - np.log(N_THRESHOLD), log_w[6] + log_per_range[BOUNDED_WIDTH_INDEX]
    )
    rule_prior = (log_w[:6] - np.log(FAMILY_SIZE))[RULE_FAMILY]
    log_joint = pt.concatenate([rule_prior, interval_prior])[None, :] + log_lik
    posterior = pt.exp(log_joint - pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    in_concept = posterior @ pt.as_tensor(CONCEPT_MEMBERSHIP)  # (sets, targets)

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)

    return {

        "row_cell": np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),

    Hessian there by central differences of the gradient, then NUTS with the
    inverse Hessian as a fixed dense mass matrix and each chain started at a
    draw of N(mode, H^-1); tuning adapts only the step size. The draws are NUTS
    draws, judged by the same gate as any fit. On the number game's seeds a fit
    took ~30 s at tune 200 / draws 250 where production NUTS took ~25 min. A
    Hessian that is not positive definite (a direction neither data nor prior
    pins down) has no metric: the fit fails, as the model's own failure.
    """
    from pymc.blocking import DictToArrayBijection, RaveledVars
    from pymc.step_methods.hmc.integration import CpuLeapfrogIntegrator
    from pymc.step_methods.hmc.quadpotential import QuadPotentialFull
    from scipy.optimize import minimize

    pm = _import_pymc()
    with model:
        step = pm.NUTS(target_accept=settings["target_accept"], max_treedepth=settings["max_treedepth"])
    # The step's own compiled log density and gradient (Jacobians in), on the
    # raveled continuous parameters: no second compile for the optimizer.
    logp_dlogp = step._logp_dlogp_func
    logp_dlogp.set_extra_values({})
    start = model.initial_point(random_seed=settings["random_seed"])
    x0 = DictToArrayBijection.map({v.name: start[v.name] for v in step.vars})
    grad = lambda x: np.asarray(logp_dlogp(x)[1], dtype=float)  # noqa: E731
    mode = minimize(lambda x: -float(logp_dlogp(x)[0]), x0.data, jac=lambda x: -grad(x), method="L-BFGS-B").x
    h = 1e-5
    hessian = np.array([(grad(mode + h * e) - grad(mode - h * e)) / (2 * h) for e in np.eye(mode.size)])
    precision = -(hessian + hessian.T) / 2

    with model:
        step = pm.NUTS(target_accept=settings["target_accept"], max_treedepth=settings["max_treedepth"])
    # The step's own compiled log density and gradient (Jacobians in), on the
    # raveled continuous parameters: no second compile for the optimizer.
    logp_dlogp = step._logp_dlogp_func
    logp_dlogp.set_extra_values({})
    start = model.initial_point(random_seed=settings["random_seed"])
    x0 = DictToArrayBijection.map({v.name: start[v.name] for v in step.vars})
    grad = lambda x: np.asarray(logp_dlogp(x)[1], dtype=float)  # noqa: E731
    mode = minimize(lambda x: -float(logp_dlogp(x)[0]), x0.data, jac=lambda x: -grad(x), method="L-BFGS-B").x
    h = 1e-5
    hessian = np.array([(grad(mode + h * e) - grad(mode - h * e)) / (2 * h) for e in np.eye(mode.size)])
    precision = -(hessian + hessian.T) / 2
    try:
        chol = np.linalg.cholesky(precision)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "warm-start NUTS: the Hessian at the posterior mode is not positive definite (some "
            "parameter direction is pinned down by neither the data nor the prior)"
        ) from None
    # The integrator holds the potential it was built with.
    step.potential = QuadPotentialFull(np.linalg.inv(precision))
    step.integrator = CpuLeapfrogIntegrator(step.potential, logp_dlogp)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(settings["random_seed"])
    starts = mode + np.linalg.solve(chol.T, rng.standard_normal((settings["chains"], mode.size)).T).T
    free = [v for v in model.unobserved_value_vars if v.name in {rv.name for rv in model.free_RVs}]
    free_values = model.compile_fn(inputs=model.value_vars, outs=free)

    def point(x: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        return {**start, **DictToArrayBijection.rmap(RaveledVars(x, x0.point_map_info))}

    with model:
        idata = pm.sample(
            draws=settings["draws"], tune=settings["tune"], chains=settings["chains"], cores=settings["cores"],
            step=step, initvals=[dict(zip([v.name for v in free], free_values(point(x)))) for x in starts],
            progressbar=False, random_seed=settings["random_seed"], idata_kwargs={"log_likelihood": True},
        )
    idata.posterior.attrs["fit_method"] = "warm_start_nuts"
    return idata

I've written a candidate called `blunted_range_size_principle`, and the admission check prints `OK` for it. It has not yet been checked for novelty against the other models, convergence over a full fit, or speed.

**Hypothesis.** People reason exactly as in the best model, `threshold_concepts_erlang_interval`, with one change: the "suspicious coincidence" that makes examples favour tight concepts is weaker for number ranges than for rules. Examples still count fully against broad rules like "even" versus "powers of 2". But their evidence against a wide range is weakened by a learned strength, `range_size_strength`: 1 gives back the best model, 0 means a range only has to cover the examples. Where it should disagree most with the best model is on several examples bunched together in size (e.g. 11, 15 or 42, 62). There this model keeps saying "yes" to targets well past the lowest and highest example, while the best model narrows onto a tight range around them. Rule-based generalisation is unchanged.

**Probe results (best-fit settings, not full sampling):**
- The fit is essentially tied with the best model: log-likelihood −2245.38 against −2245.33.
- The fitted strength is 0.85, and the typical range width drops from 66 to 45. I checked the strength is pinned down by the data: fixing it at 0.5 costs 11 nats, and at 0 costs 52.
- Its predictions differ from the best model's by 0.009 (RMSE) on the novelty pool, above the 0.002 near-duplicate cutoff.

**Ideas I tried first that went nowhere** (each fell back to the best model or fit worse; logged in memory):
- Weak sampling for all rules, or only for digit rules.
- "Within d of an example" concepts.
- Ranges whose edges fall only on multiples of 5 (17 nats worse).
- Doubling and tripling chains.
- A belief that the program favours small numbers.

**Speed risk.** The smoke fit took 279 s for 200 iterations. That was on a heavily loaded machine, with a second copy of the check running at the same time by mistake for part of it. Each gradient costs about 0.06 s. I tried a version that groups ranges by width, but it was slower (0.15 s), so I kept the original. With the warm-start sampler and its default run lengths, a full fit should take a few minutes, well inside the 30-minute limit, but I haven't measured that.
